summary: Prothous (Ancient Greek: Πρόθοος) was son of Tenthredon and commander of the Magnetes in the Trojan War. Homer places his people about the river Peneius and forested Mount Pelion; he brings forty black ships to Troy. Later authors disagree whether he died in the shipwreck off Cape Caphereus or settled in Libya with Eurypylus and Guneus.

sections.heading: Magnetes at Troy
paragraphs: The Catalogue of Ships names Prothous son of Tenthredon leader of the Magnetes who dwelt about fair-flowing Peneius and Pelion covered with waving forests. Forty black ships followed the swift captain. Hyginus and Apollodorus repeat him among the Greek leaders; mother-names in the mythographers include Eurymache or Cleobule daughter of Eurytus.

He belongs to the Thessalian muster beside other northern lords who sailed to Ilios — a Homeric captain whose personal aristeia is thin, but whose Catalogue entry fixes Magnesia on the map of the war.

sections.heading: Returns and homonyms
paragraphs: Post-Homeric returns disagree: one version has Prothous perish with Meges and others in the wreck near Cape Caphereus of Euboea; another sends Prothous, Eurypylus, and Guneus to Libya, where they settle.

This atlas entry (prothous-magnesia) is Tenthredon's Magnetes captain — not the Arcadian son of Lycaon, not Althaea's Calydonian brother, not Agrius' Aetolian son, not the Theban-cycle warriors, and not the Suitors of Penelope from Same (prothous-same).
